question:
Which of the following peptides has been found to bind or is highly likely to bind an integrin receptor in an in vitro assay?

Answer Choices:
A. RGDMAA
B. RGDSPSS
C. RGDLTTP
D. RGDQVSK
E. RGDARGG

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

All five peptides contain the canonical Arg-Gly-Asp integrin recognition motif, but integrin recognition is strongly context dependent. The high affinity α5β1/αvβ3 ligand of fibronectin is the GRGDSP[X] motif. The minimal cell adhesive sequence of fibronectin type III10 is GRGDSPASSKP and the synthetic peptide GRGDSP is the classic integrin mimetic. 

RGDSPSS is essentially the RGDSP core of fibronectin with an additional Ser-Ser extension, RGD-S-P-S-S, i.e. the RGD followed by Ser-Pro that is the well characterized integrin binding context. Proline in the +2 to +4 position relative to Asp and the Ser-Pro motif increase affinity for α5β1 and αvβ3 in vitro and the peptide is routinely used as a fibronectin-derived integrin ligand.

RGDMAA, RGDLTTP, RGDQVSK and RGDARGG lack the canonical fibronectin Ser-Pro flanking context and are not the established high affinity RGD integrin ligands; in particular the RGDSP core is the one that has been repeatedly demonstrated to bind α5β1, αvβ3 and related RGD-binding integrins in in vitro cell adhesion, solid-phase binding and competition assays. That is the peptide that is most likely to be a functional integrin binder in the set.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

The integrin ligand core is the RGD tripeptide Arg-Gly-Asp and the activity is strongly modulated by the C-terminal flanking residues. The classical fibronectin type III 10 cell-binding site is
...GRGDSPASSKP...
and the minimal high affinity sequence for α5β1 and αvβ3 integrins is RGDSP. 

RGDSPSS contains the canonical RGDSP motif at its N-terminus. The RGDSP sequence places a Pro in the +3 position relative to Arg which nucleates the β-turn required for presentation of the RGD loop to the integrin binding pocket, and the adjacent Ser residues mimic the fibronectin RGDSPASSKP context that is the archetypal in vitro integrin binder.

The other peptides lack this fibronectin-like context and the RGD is in sequences that are not reported as high-affinity integrin ligands in vitro. RGDSPSS is therefore the peptide that has been found, and is expected, to bind integrins in an in vitro assay.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

The canonical integrin ligand is the RGD triad and integrin specificity is largely set by the flanking sequence, in particular the +1 and +2 positions relative to RGD.

RGDSPSS is the classic fibronectin type III10-like context. The natural fibronectin integrin-binding site is

...RGDSPASSKP...

i.e. RGD-S-P-...  The peptide RGDSPSS retains the RGD-S-P core that is required for high-affinity binding to α5β1 and αvβ3 family integrins in vitro, with the +1 Ser and +2 Pro being the consensus fibronectin flanking that maintains the extended loop conformation recognised by the integrin headpiece. RGDSP and RGDSPASS-derived peptides are the prototypical synthetic integrin mimetics used in vitro and in biomaterials.

RGDMAA, RGDLTTP, RGDQVSK and RGDARGG all contain an RGD motif but have non-consensus flanking that is not the fibronectin/vitronectin consensus and has not been reported as a high-affinity integrin ligand in vitro. The Ser-Pro flanking of RGDSPSS makes it the highly likely functional integrin binder of the set.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

All of the peptides contain the canonical RGD integrin recognition motif, but integrin binding in vitro is strongly dependent on the RGD flanking sequence and the presentation of the loop. The prototypical high–affinity fibronectin integrin ligand is the type III10 loop

GRGDSPASSKP

and the minimal active core is RGDSP.  RGDSPSS is essentially a truncated copy of that fibronectin loop, RGD–S–P, with the +1 Ser and +2 Pro that are known to be required for α5β1 and αvβ3 recognition and to stabilise the RGD in the extended conformation needed for binding. The same RGDSP motif is the basis of the classic synthetic ligands GRGDSP, GRGDSPASS and related GRGDSP-X peptides that are routinely used as positive integrin-binding controls in adhesion, solid-phase binding and cell-spreading assays.

RGDMAA, RGDLTTP, RGDQVSK and RGDARGG carry non-canonical flanking residues at +1/+2/+3 and have either been shown to be weak/non-binding controls or are not homologous to known high-affinity natural ligands. The Ser-Pro-containing RGDSPSS is therefore the sequence that is homologous to a bona fide integrin-binding natural site and is highly likely to retain integrin binding in an in vitro assay.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

The strongest choice is RGDSPSS because it contains the RGDSP sequence, which is closely related to the canonical fibronectin-derived integrin-binding motif. Short RGDSP-containing peptides are widely used in in vitro integrin-binding/adhesion assays, especially for α5β1 and αvβ3, because the flanking Ser/Pro residues help present the RGD motif in a favorable conformation. While the other peptides also contain RGD, RGDSPSS has the most established and commonly assayed integrin-binding context.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

All five peptides contain the canonical RGD integrin recognition motif.  In vitro integrin recognition of RGD is strongly dependent on the immediate flanking sequence and on the ability to present the RGD in an extended / β-turn conformation. The classic high-affinity fibronectin cell-binding domain is

… R G D S P A S S K P …

i.e. RGD-S-P. The Ser-Pro pair is the structural determinant that places the RGD in the correct conformation for α5β1 and αvβ3 and related RGD-binding integrins. 

RGDSPSS = R G D S P S S retains the RGDSP core, RGD-S-P, of the fibronectin type III10 cell-binding site, RGDSPASSKP, with a conservative Ala→Ser substitution at +6. The motif is therefore essentially the fibronectin RGDSP motif and is a well documented/ highly probable integrin ligand in vitro. The other sequences lack the canonical RGDSP / RGDSPAS context and/or the Pro-constrained turn, e.g. RGDMAA, RGDQVSK and RGDARGG are commonly used as low / non-binding RGD controls, and RGDLTTP places the Pro too distal and lacks the Ser-Pro turn.

Hence RGDSPSS is the peptide most likely to bind / is known to bind an RGD-recognising integrin in an in vitro assay.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

The RGD tripeptide is the minimal recognition motif for the RGD-binding integrins α5β1, αvβ3, αvβ5, αvβ6 etc. Binding in vitro is strongly dependent on the conformation and the flanking residues that present the RGD loop.

RGDSPSS contains the canonical fibronectin cell-binding motif RGDSP. The natural fibronectin type III10 cell-binding domain is  ...P R G D S P A S S K P... and the minimal high-affinity synthetic ligand is GRGDSP. RGDSPSS is essentially RGDSP with the same Ser/Pro-rich, flexible N-cap that presents the RGD loop in the extended conformation recognised by α5β1 fibronectin receptor and by αvβ3/vitronectin receptors in vitro.

RGDMAA, RGDQVSK and RGDARGG have flanking sequences that deviate from the well-characterised RGDSP/ RGDV type presentation and are not the published fibronectin/vitronectin-derived high-affinity ligands. RGDLTTP is a leucine/threonine flanked motif and is a weaker / context-dependent ligand in comparison with the fibronectin-derived RGDSPxx series. The RGDSPSS sequence is therefore the one that has been found and is highly likely to bind an RGD integrin in an in vitro assay.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

The RGD motif is essential, but the flanking residues strongly influence whether the peptide adopts a conformation that integrins can recognize. RGDSPSS contains the RGDSP core, which is very close to the classic fibronectin-derived GRGDSP sequence used in many integrin-binding assays. The Ser-Pro segment can promote a turn that presents the RGD motif appropriately to integrin receptors such as α5β1 and αvβ3. The other options have less canonical flanking sequences and are less likely to support strong integrin binding in vitro.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

The RGD motif is the canonical integrin recognition sequence and its affinity/specificity is strongly set by the flanking residues. The fibronectin type III10 integrin binding site is

…P R G D S P A S S K P…

and the minimal active core is RGDSP, classically used as GRGDSP / GRGDSPASS for α5β1 and αvβ3 binding in vitro.

RGDSPSS is essentially the fibronectin RGDSP core with a serine-for-alanine substitution at the +4 position, R G D S P S S. The RGDSP sequence is preserved and the Ser/Pro rich C-terminus is the one found in the natural high-affinity ligand. In contrast RGDMAA, RGDLTTP, RGDQVSK and RGDARGG lack the optimal Ser-Pro context that is required for high-affinity integrin engagement and are not recognised natural RGD integrin ligands; they are routinely used as low/negative controls. Hence the fibronectin-like peptide RGDSPSS is the one that has been found and is highly likely to bind integrins, e.g. α5β1 and αvβ3, in an in vitro adhesion / binding assay.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. RGDSPSS

All five sequences contain the canonical RGD core, but integrin recognition is strongly context dependent. The best characterised high affinity α5β1/αvβ3 ligand is the fibronectin type III10 RGD loop

GRGDSPASSKP

and the minimal functional unit is RGDSP with a Ser at +2 and a Pro at +3 relative to the RGD motif which stabilises the β-turn that is presented to the integrin metal ion dependent adhesion site.

RGDSPSS = RGD-S-P-S-S

contains the canonical RGDSP core intact at the N-terminus, Ser +2 Pro +3, exactly the fibronectin-derived motif that is used routinely in vitro as a positive integrin α5β1/αvβ3 ligand. The C-terminal SS extension is tolerated and is in fact present in the naturally occurring fibronectin sequence.

RGDMAA, RGDLTTP, RGDQVSK and RGDARGG all place non-optimal side chains at +2/+3 and lack the RGDSP/Pro-turn context. RGDMAA is in particular used in the literature as a RGD-scrambled / non-binding control, and RGDLTTP, RGDQVSK and RGDARGG are poor / non-binding analogues in standard cell adhesion, solid phase binding and inhibition assays. B is therefore the sequence that has been found to bind and is the textbook example of a highly likely integrin binder.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about which RGD-containing peptide is known/highly likely to bind an integrin in vitro. All five peptides contain the canonical RGD motif, but binding is context dependent and set by flanking residues.

Current best answer is B. RGDSPSS.

Evidence accumulating from colleagues:
- Canonical high-affinity RGD integrin ligand is fibronectin type III10: ...PRGDSPASSKP..., minimal active core RGDSP, classically used as GRGDSP / GRGDSPASS for α5β1 and αvβ3 binding in vitro.
- RGDSPSS = RGD-S-P-S-S retains the RGDSP core intact at the N-terminus, i.e. Ser at +1/+2 and Pro at +3 relative to RGD, the Ser-Pro turn that stabilises the β-turn/ extended loop presented to the integrin metal ion dependent adhesion site.
- This is essentially a truncated fibronectin loop with a conservative extension; the C-terminal SS is tolerated and mimics the fibronectin ASSKP context.
- The peptide is routinely used as a positive fibronectin-derived integrin mimetic in adhesion, solid-phase binding, cell spreading and competition assays.

Other options:
- RGDMAA, RGDLTTP, RGDQVSK, RGDARGG lack the canonical RGDSP / Ser-Pro context, have non-consensus +1/+2/+3 flanking, and are described in literature as weak/non-binding controls or poor integrin ligands. RGDMAA in particular is cited as a non-binding control.
- RGDLTTP places Pro too distal and lacks Ser-Pro turn.

Colleague consensus in round 0 is unanimous for B. No dissent or alternative candidates proposed. No errors or corrections noted yet.

Unresolved / to watch: exact in vitro assay specificity for each integrin subtype, but the relative ranking is clear: B >> others.

Current belief: B is the peptide found to / highly likely to bind an integrin receptor in vitro.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: All nine colleagues in round 0 converge on answer B. RGDSPSS.

Consensus rationale:
- All peptides contain RGD, but integrin binding in vitro is strongly context-dependent on flanking residues and conformation.
- Canonical high-affinity fibronectin type III10 ligand is ...PRGDSPASSKP..., minimal active core RGDSP, classic synthetic ligand GRGDSP / GRGDSPASS.
- RGDSPSS = R G D S P S S retains the RGD-S-P core with +1 Ser and +2 Pro relative to Asp, i.e. the Ser-Pro turn that stabilises the β-turn/extended loop presented to the MIDAS site of α5β1, αvβ3 and related RGD-binding integrins. This is essentially a truncated fibronectin loop, with the C-terminal SS tolerated/mimicking the natural ASSKP extension.
- RGDSP motif is routinely used as a positive integrin-binding control in adhesion, solid-phase binding, competition and cell-spreading assays.

Competing options judged unlikely:
- RGDMAA, RGDQVSK, RGDARGG lack the canonical RGDSP/Ser-Pro context; RGDMAA in particular is cited as a non-binding/scrambled control.
- RGDLTTP places Pro too distal, lacks Ser-Pro turn, leucine/threonine flanked, weaker/context-dependent.

No dissent or alternative answer proposed in round 0; all colleagues give B with essentially the same mechanistic explanation. My current belief aligns with B, with high confidence based on unanimous expert reasoning and the established fibronectin RGDSP literature. Unresolved: none material; if needed, specific quantitative affinity differences among the non-canonical peptides could be clarified, but not required for choice.

The Ser at +2 and Pro at +3 relative to RGD stabilise the turn required for the integrin metal-ion-dependent adhesion site.

RGDSPSS = RGD-S-P-S-S retains the RGDSP core intact at the N-terminus, i.e. RGD followed by Ser-Pro, essentially a truncated fibronectin-like loop with a Ser/Pro-rich C-terminus. This matches the well-documented fibronectin-derived integrin ligand and is cited as routinely used as a positive integrin-binding control.

Current belief: B is highly likely / known to bind RGD-recognising integrins such as α5β1, αvβ3 in vitro, consistent with consensus evidence. Unresolved questions: none apparent for this round; the unanimity suggests low uncertainty.

All five sequences contain the RGD triad, but RGD-binding integrin recognition in vitro is set by flanking context and the ability to present RGD in the extended β-turn recognised by the MIDAS of α5β1, αvβ3, αvβ5 etc.

The prototypical high-affinity ligand is fibronectin type III10 …PRGDSPASSKP… with minimal active core RGDSP. GRGDSP / GRGDSPASS and RGDSP-X peptides are the textbook positive controls for α5β1/αvβ3 adhesion, solid-phase binding, cell spreading and competition assays. The +1 Ser and +2 Pro relative to Asp, RGD-S-P, nucleate the Ser-Pro turn that stabilises the fibronectin-like loop.

RGDSPSS = R-G-D-S-P-S-S retains the canonical RGDSP core intact at the N-terminus, i.e. Ser +1 and Pro +2, the Ser-Pro turn of the fibronectin cell-binding loop. It is essentially a truncated RGDSPASSKP-like sequence with a tolerated Ser-Ser C-terminal extension and is homologous to a bona fide natural integrin-binding site.

RGDMAA is a classic low/non-binding RGD control; RGDLTTP places Pro too distal and lacks the Ser-Pro +1/+2 turn; RGDQVSK and RGDARGG have non-consensus +1/+2/+3 flanking and no Pro-constrained Ser-Pro turn. None of them match the fibronectin/vitronectin RGDSP consensus used as in vitro positive ligands.

Hence RGDSPSS is the fibronectin-derived sequence that has been found and is highly likely to bind RGD-recognising integrins, e.g. α5β1 and αvβ3, in an in vitro assay.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B, RGDSPSS, still seems the most defensible in a generic in vitro integrin-binding context. The key is that all candidates have RGD, so the discriminator is the immediate C-terminal presentation. RGDSPSS preserves the canonical RGD-S-P core, with Ser at +1 and Pro at +2 relative to Asp, which is the minimal fibronectin type III10 cell-binding motif and the basis of classic GRGDSP/GRGDSPASS positive-control peptides for RGD-binding integrins such as α5β1 and αvβ3. So I would not shift away from B based on the current discussion.

All 10 colleagues remain unanimous across rounds 0, 1 and 2 on B. RGDSPSS as the peptide found / highly likely to bind an integrin receptor in an in vitro assay. No dissent or alternative answer has been proposed in round 2.

Core claim retained: RGD is necessary but not sufficient; in vitro binding by RGD-recognising integrins α5β1, αvβ3, αvβ5 etc. is context dependent on flanking residues and the β-turn/ extended loop presentation to the MIDAS. 1.text:
B. RGDSPSS

All five peptides contain the RGD triad, but RGD-binding integrin engagement in vitro is context dependent and requires presentation of RGD in the extended β-turn recognised by the MIDAS of RGD-recognising integrins such as α5β1, αvβ3 and αvβ5.

The archetypal high affinity natural ligand is fibronectin type III10 …PRGDSPASSKP… with minimal active core RGDSP. GRGDSP/GRGDSPASS and the RGDSP-X series are the classic in vitro positive controls for adhesion, solid-phase binding, cell spreading and competition assays. The +1 Ser and +2 Pro relative to Asp, RGD-S-P, nucleate the Ser-Pro turn that stabilises the loop presented to the integrin headpiece.

RGDSPSS = R-G-D-S-P-S-S retains the canonical RGDSP core intact at the N-terminus, i.e. Ser +1 and Pro +2 relative to Asp. It is essentially a truncated fibronectin loop RGDSPASSKP → RGDSPSS with a tolerated Ser-Ser C-terminal extension and is functionally homologous to the textbook fibronectin-derived integrin mimetic.

RGDMAA is routinely used as a low/non-binding RGD scrambled control. RGDLTTP places Pro too distal, +1/+2 = Leu-Thr not Ser-Pro, and lacks the canonical Ser-Pro turn. RGDQVSK and RGDARGG have non-consensus +1/+2/+3 flanking and lack the fibronectin/vitronectin RGDSP motif.

RGDSPSS is therefore the fibronectin-like sequence that has been found and is highly likely to bind an RGD-recognising integrin, e.g. α5β1/αvβ3, in an in vitro assay.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I would still stay with B, RGDSPSS. The important distinction is not whether an RGD-containing peptide can bind some integrin under some specialized conditions, but which sequence is best supported as a generic in vitro RGD-binding integrin ligand. I would not shift from B on the current evidence.

B. RGDSPSS

All five peptides contain the RGD triad but RGD-integrin engagement in vitro is context dependent on presentation of the motif in an extended β-turn recognised by the MIDAS of α5β1, αvβ3, αvβ5 etc.

RGDSPSS is therefore the fibronectin-derived sequence that has been found and is highly likely to bind RGD-recognising integrins, e.g. α5β1/αvβ3, in an in vitro assay.

I remain with B, RGDSPSS. The key issue is not whether an RGDL-containing peptide can ever engage an integrin in a subtype-selective context; it can. But for an unspecified in vitro integrin-binding assay, the strongest and most established RGD presentation is the fibronectin-type RGDSP core. * Best characterised high-affinity natural ligand is fibronectin type III10 …P R G D S P A S S K P…, minimal active core RGDSP. Synthetic GRGDSP / GRGDSPASS are textbook positive controls in adhesion, solid-phase binding, competition assays.
